from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout("The Cast of Characters", [
            "Mathematics features five fundamental, seemingly unrelated constants.",
            "Meet zero, one, e, the imaginary i, and pi.",
            "Today, we unite these different worlds in one equation."
        ])

        # Initial focus setup: Start with first line active, others dimmed
        self.lecture.set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Visualizing the introduction
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Transition lecture focus
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(GRAY),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE)
        )

        # Replacing MathTex with Text to avoid FileNotFoundError: 'latex'
        # Constants and specific colors: {0: #FFD700, 1: #00FF00, e: #00BFFF, i: #FF00FF, pi: #FFA500}
        c_zero = Text("0", color="#FFD700")
        c_one = Text("1", color="#00FF00")
        c_e = Text("e", color="#00BFFF", slant=ITALIC)
        c_i = Text("i", color="#FF00FF", slant=ITALIC)
        c_pi = Text("π", color="#FFA500")

        # Labels for each constant with matching colors
        l_arithmetic = Text("Arithmetic", font_size=24, color="#FFD700")
        l_identity = Text("Identity", font_size=24, color="#00FF00")
        l_calculus = Text("Calculus", font_size=24, color="#00BFFF")
        l_imaginary = Text("Imaginary", font_size=24, color="#FF00FF")
        l_geometry = Text("Geometry", font_size=24, color="#FFA500")

        # Position characters using the grid system (right side focus)
        self.place_at_grid(c_zero, "B2", scale_factor=2.0)
        self.place_at_grid(l_arithmetic, "C2", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        self.place_at_grid(c_one, "B5", scale_factor=2.0)
        self.place_at_grid(l_identity, "C5", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        self.place_at_grid(c_e, "D2", scale_factor=2.0)
        self.place_at_grid(l_calculus, "E2", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        self.place_at_grid(c_i, "D5", scale_factor=2.0)
        self.place_at_grid(l_imaginary, "E5", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        self.place_at_grid(c_pi, "E4", scale_factor=2.0)
        self.place_at_grid(l_geometry, "F4", scale_factor=0.6)

        # Animation: Constants and their labels appear
        self.play(
            FadeIn(c_zero), FadeIn(l_arithmetic),
            FadeIn(c_one), FadeIn(l_identity),
            FadeIn(c_e), FadeIn(l_calculus),
            FadeIn(c_i), FadeIn(l_imaginary),
            FadeIn(c_pi), FadeIn(l_geometry),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Transition lecture focus
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GRAY),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE)
        )

        # Unification: Calculate center horizontal arrangement
        target_group = VGroup(
            c_e.copy(), 
            c_i.copy(), 
            c_pi.copy(), 
            c_one.copy(), 
            c_zero.copy()
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.6)
        
        # Center the group in the available right-side space (B2 to E5 area)
        self.place_in_area(target_group, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=1.2)

        # Animate constants merging to center as labels fade out
        self.play(
            FadeOut(l_arithmetic),
            FadeOut(l_identity),
            FadeOut(l_calculus),
            FadeOut(l_imaginary),
            FadeOut(l_geometry),
            c_e.animate.move_to(target_group[0]),
            c_i.animate.move_to(target_group[1]),
            c_pi.animate.move_to(target_group[2]),
            c_one.animate.move_to(target_group[3]),
            c_zero.animate.move_to(target_group[4]),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with title and lecture lines

            [
                "Forget 'impossible'; think of i as a spatial turn.",

            ]
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        # Draw a white horizontal number line. 
        # Using grid points D1 to D6 to span the right-side area.

        # Place a green dot at the position '1' (grid D5, with origin at D3)

        pos_1 = self.grid["D5"]
        dot = Dot(pos_1, color="#00FF00")
        
        self.play(Create(h_axis))
        self.play(FadeIn(dot))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Reset previous line and highlight current line in magenta
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF00FF")
        
        # Define the rotation arc (radius 2 grid units, from D5 to B3 around D3)

            radius=2.0, 
            start_angle=0, 
            angle=PI/2, 
            arc_center=origin_point, 
            color="#FF00FF"
        )
        
        # Animate the dot rotating 90 degrees CCW
        self.play(
            Create(arc), 
            Rotate(dot, angle=PI/2, about_point=origin_point), 
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Reset previous line and highlight current line in magenta
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF00FF")
        
        # Draw the vertical axis through the origin (A3 to F3)
        v_axis = Line(self.grid["A3"], self.grid["F3"], color=WHITE)
        
        # Label the new vertical position as 'i'
        label_i = Text("i", font_size=32, color="#FF00FF")

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial layout setup
        title_text = "Exponential Growth vs. Circular Motion"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Normally, e to the x represents continuous linear growth.",
            "But adding i creates a constant sideways push.",
            "This perpendicular force turns straight growth into a curve.",
            "Continuous sideways motion forms a perfect circular path.",
            "Linear expansion transforms into elegant, eternal rotation."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Visual anchors using the 6x6 grid
        origin_center = self.grid['D3']
        start_point = self.grid['D4']
        
        # Colors from the animation plan
        BLUE_DOT_COLOR = "#00BFFF"
        MAGENTA_VEC_COLOR = "#FF00FF"
        WHITE_ARC_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE_DOT_COLOR))
        
        dot = Dot(color=BLUE_DOT_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(dot, 'D4')
        
        # Using Text instead of MathTex to avoid LaTeX dependency issues
        growth_label = Text("e^x", color=BLUE_DOT_COLOR, font_size=24)
        growth_label.move_to(start_point + UP * 0.4)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(dot), FadeIn(growth_label))
        
        self.play(
            dot.animate.move_to(self.grid['D6']),
            growth_label.animate.move_to(self.grid['D6'] + UP * 0.4),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(MAGENTA_VEC_COLOR))
        
        self.play(
            dot.animate.move_to(start_point),
            growth_label.animate.move_to(start_point + UP * 0.4),
            run_time=1
        )
        
        i_vec = Arrow(start=start_point, end=self.grid['C4'], color=MAGENTA_VEC_COLOR, buff=0)
        i_label = Text("i", color=MAGENTA_VEC_COLOR, font_size=32)
        i_label.move_to(self.grid['C4'] + UR * 0.2)
        
        self.play(GrowArrow(i_vec), Write(i_label))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE_ARC_COLOR))
        
        arc_path = TracedPath(dot.get_center, stroke_color=WHITE_ARC_COLOR, stroke_width=4)
        self.add(arc_path)
        
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(
            origin_center + np.array([np.cos(angle_tracker.get_value()), np.sin(angle_tracker.get_value()), 0])
        ))
        
        def update_i_vec(v):
            pos = dot.get_center()
            angle = angle_tracker.get_value()
            tangent_dir = np.array([-np.sin(angle), np.cos(angle), 0])
            v.become(Arrow(start=pos, end=pos + tangent_dir, color=MAGENTA_VEC_COLOR, buff=0))
        
        i_vec.add_updater(update_i_vec)
        i_label.add_updater(lambda l: l.next_to(i_vec.get_end(), UR, buff=0.1))
        
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(PI/2), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(BLUE_DOT_COLOR))
        
        circular_label = Text("e^ix", color=BLUE_DOT_COLOR, font_size=28)
        circular_label.add_updater(lambda l: l.next_to(dot, UR, buff=0.1))
        
        self.play(FadeOut(growth_label), FadeIn(circular_label))
        
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(PI), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE_ARC_COLOR))
        
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(2*PI), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
        
        dot.clear_updaters()
        i_vec.clear_updaters()
        i_label.clear_updaters()
        circular_label.clear_updaters()
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with title and lecture lines
        # Using Text instead of MathTex to avoid LaTeX dependency
        self.setup_layout("The Half-Circle Journey (e^iπ)", [
            "Let's set our angle x to exactly pi radians.",
            "Pi represents a journey halfway around the circle's edge.",
            "Starting at 1, a 180-degree turn lands us at -1."
        ])

        # Visualization logic
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True}
        )
        self.place_in_area(plane, "B3", "F6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        circle = Circle(radius=plane.get_x_unit_size(), color=BLUE_E)
        circle.move_to(plane.get_origin())
        
        dot = Dot(plane.coords_to_point(1, 0), color=YELLOW)
        path = Arc(radius=plane.get_x_unit_size(), start_angle=0, angle=PI, color=YELLOW)
        path.move_to(plane.get_origin(), aligned_edge=LEFT) # Adjusting arc position
        path.shift(RIGHT * plane.get_x_unit_size() / 2) # Manual alignment to center
        path.move_to(plane.get_origin()) # Re-centering properly
        
        label_1 = Text("1", font_size=20).next_to(plane.coords_to_point(1, 0), DOWN)
        label_minus_1 = Text("-1", font_size=20).next_to(plane.coords_to_point(-1, 0), DOWN)

        self.add(plane, circle, dot, label_1, label_minus_1)
        
        self.play(
            MoveAlongPath(dot, path),
            run_time=3,
            rate_func=slow_into
        )
        self.wait(2)

        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Grand Reunion: e^i\u03c0 + 1 = 0", ["Add one to both sides to reach perfect balance.", "Growth, rotation, and geometry finally meet at zero.", "Euler's identity: the most beautiful equation in all mathematics."])
        # 1. Setup Layout and Title
        # Using MarkupText as it allows for simple HTML-like formatting for exponents
        title = MarkupText("The Grand Reunion: e<sup>iπ</sup> + 1 = 0", font_size=36, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)

        # 2. Equation Definitions
        # Replacing MathTex with VGroups of MarkupText to avoid FileNotFoundError: 'latex'
        # Indices: 0: "e^{iπ}", 1: "=", 2: "-1"
        eq1 = VGroup(MarkupText("e<sup>iπ</sup>"), MarkupText("="), MarkupText("-1"), color=WHITE).arrange(RIGHT).move_to(ORIGIN)

        # eq2 represents: e^{iπ} + 1 = 0
        # Indices: 0: "e^{iπ}", 1: "+", 2: "1", 3: "=", 4: "0"
        eq2 = VGroup(MarkupText("e<sup>iπ</sup>"), MarkupText("+"), MarkupText("1"), MarkupText("="), MarkupText("0"), color=WHITE).arrange(RIGHT).move_to(ORIGIN)
        
        # Apply specific colors to the final identity result
        eq2[3].set_color(GOLD)  # The '=' sign
        eq2[4].set_color(GOLD)  # The '0'

        # 3. Animation Sequence
        # Display the Title
        self.play(Write(title))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Display the starting equation e^{iπ} = -1
        self.play(Write(eq1))

outline.topic: The Most Beautiful Formula: Demystifying Euler's Identity (e^(iπ) = -1)
outline.target_audience: Advanced High School Students and Early University Students

sections.title: The Cast of Characters
sections.content: Introduce the five fundamental constants of mathematics: 0, 1, e, i, and π. Present them as seemingly unrelated 'characters' from different worlds (arithmetic, calculus, complex numbers, and geometry) that are about to be united in one single equation.
sections.example: Visualize five distinct islands floating in space, each representing a number. A cosmic bridge begins to form between them as the narrator speaks.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Magic of 'i' as a Turn
sections.content: Redefine the imaginary unit 'i' not just as √-1, but as a geometric operator. Multiplying by 'i' represents a 90-degree counter-clockwise rotation on the complex plane. This shifts the perspective from 'impossible math' to 'spatial orientation'.
sections.example: An ant (the character) walking on a number line. When it hits the 'i' operation, instead of moving forward or backward, it turns left and walks into the 2D 'Complex Plane'.

sections.title: Exponential Growth vs. Circular Motion
sections.content: Explain that e^x usually represents continuous growth in a straight line. However, when the exponent becomes 'ix', the 'growth' is constantly pushed sideways by the rotational power of 'i'. This transforms linear growth into a perfect circular path.
sections.example: A drone flying at a constant speed. If it flies straight, it's 'e^x'. If a side-wind (represented by 'i') constantly pushes it perpendicular to its path, it starts flying in a perfect circle around the origin.

sections.title: Euler's Formula: The GPS of the Complex Plane
sections.content: Introduce the general formula e^(ix) = cos(x) + i sin(x). Explain that any point on the Unit Circle can be reached by choosing the right angle 'x' (in radians). Show the visual connection between the exponential form and the trigonometric coordinates.
sections.example: A radar screen where a pulsing dot (e^ix) moves along a circular boundary. The horizontal position is cos(x) and the vertical position is sin(x).

sections.title: The Half-Circle Journey (e^iπ)
sections.content: Apply the angle π (180 degrees) to the formula. If we travel π radians around the circle, we end up exactly on the opposite side of the starting point (1). This location on the complex plane is -1.
sections.example: A character starts at position '1' on a giant clock face. They walk halfway around the edge (a distance of π). When they stop, the label on the floor says '-1'.

sections.title: The Grand Reunion: e^iπ + 1 = 0
sections.content: Conclude by adding 1 to both sides to reach the final identity. Summarize how the formula links growth (e), rotation (i), and geometry (π) to reach the balance of zero.
sections.example: The five floating islands from Section 1 finally lock together like puzzle pieces, forming a glowing ring that hums in perfect harmony, symbolizing the unity of mathematics.

storyboard.title: The Cast of Characters
lecture_lines: Mathematics features five fundamental, seemingly unrelated constants.
Meet zero, one, e, the imaginary i, and pi.
Today, we unite these different worlds in one equation.
animations: Fade in the five constants {0: #FFD700, 1: #00FF00, e: #00BFFF, i: #FF00FF, pi: #FFA500} in distinct colors at different screen positions.
Add text labels 'Arithmetic', 'Identity', 'Calculus', 'Imaginary', 'Geometry' below each respective constant.
Animate all five constants moving toward the center of the screen as the labels fade out.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: The Magic of 'i' as a Turn
lecture_lines: Forget 'impossible'; think of i as a spatial turn.
Multiplying by i rotates a number ninety degrees counter-clockwise.
This shifts our view from lines to the complex plane.
animations: Draw a white (#FFFFFF) horizontal number line with a green dot (#00FF00) at the position '1'.
Animate the dot rotating 90 degrees counter-clockwise along a magenta (#FF00FF) arc to the vertical axis.
Label the new vertical position as 'i' (#FF00FF) and show the text 'x i = +90 rotation' nearby.

storyboard.title: Exponential Growth vs. Circular Motion
lecture_lines: Normally, e to the x represents continuous linear growth.
But adding i creates a constant sideways push.
This perpendicular force turns straight growth into a curve.
Continuous sideways motion forms a perfect circular path.
Linear expansion transforms into elegant, eternal rotation.
animations: Show a blue dot (#00BFFF) at (1,0) starting to move horizontally to represent standard growth.
Introduce a magenta vector (#FF00FF) labeled 'i' acting perpendicularly to the dot's current velocity.
The dot's path bends into a circular arc (#FFFFFF) as the 'i' force acts like a steering wheel.
Highlight the moving dot with the label 'e^(ix)' (#00BFFF) as it continues its circular path.
Complete the unit circle, illustrating how imaginary growth creates rotation instead of distance.

storyboard.title: Euler's Formula: The GPS of the Complex Plane
lecture_lines: Euler's formula defines our position on this circular path.
e to the i x equals cosine x plus i sine x.
Choosing an angle x places us on the unit circle.
Cosine tracks horizontal position, while sine tracks the vertical.
It is the ultimate GPS for the complex plane.
animations: Display the formula 'e^(ix) = cos(x) + i sin(x)' (#FFFFFF) at the top of the screen.
Show a white unit circle with an orange (#FFA500) radius vector at an arbitrary angle 'x'.
Draw a green dashed line (#00FF00) to the x-axis, labeled 'cos(x)'.
Draw a magenta dashed line (#FF00FF) to the y-axis, labeled 'i sin(x)'.
Animate the dot moving along the circle, showing the x and y components updating in real-time.

storyboard.title: The Half-Circle Journey (e^iπ)
lecture_lines: Let's set our angle x to exactly pi radians.
Pi represents a journey halfway around the circle's edge.
Starting at one, we rotate one hundred eighty degrees.
Our path leads us directly to the value negative one.
Thus, e to the i pi equals negative one.
animations: Start with the formula 'e^(ix)' and substitute 'x' with 'pi' (#FFA500).
On the unit circle, animate the point moving from '1' (#00FF00) along the top edge.
Highlight the arc as it covers exactly 180 degrees (pi radians).
The point lands on the far left side, labeled with a large '-1' (#FFD700).
Write the simplified equation 'e^(i pi) = -1' (#FFFFFF) in the center of the screen.

storyboard.title: The Grand Reunion: e^iπ + 1 = 0
lecture_lines: Add one to both sides to reach perfect balance.
Growth, rotation, and geometry finally meet at zero.
Euler's identity: the most beautiful equation in all mathematics.
animations: Show the equation 'e^(i pi) = -1' (#FFFFFF) isolated on screen.
Animate the '-1' moving to the left side of the equals sign, transforming into '+ 1'.
The equation 'e^(i pi) + 1 = 0' appears, with '0' (#FFD700) appearing on the right to balance it.
